title: Intimidation — Threats of 'More Problems' if Authorities Are Called

confidence.derivation_formula: value = round( sum_per_article( applicability_weight × element_grid.weighted_score ) / sum_of_weights × authorities_verification_factor, 2 ); authorities_verification_factor = 0.85 + 0.15 × verified_ratio = 0.850

allegation_summary: STG-6 documents intimidation tactics by LATAM security personnel, including: (1) Explicit threats of 'more problems' if passenger involves authorities; (2) Coercive language designed to discourage legal resistance; (3) Use of security personnel to create atmosphere of threat; (4) Systematic effort to isolate passenger from external protections. These intimidation tactics violate: (a) Chilean Penal Code Art. 296 prohibitions on threats and coercion; (b) ICAO Annex 9 §8.15 requirements for non-coercive complaint resolution; (c) Chilean consumer protection law prohibitions on abusive practices; (d) International standards on passenger treatment in aviation.

articles.article_name: Codigo Penal (CHIPENCOD), Art. 211 — Imputacion falsa de crimen o simple delito
articles.article_text: El que imputare falsamente a alguna persona haber cometido un crimen o simple delito, siendo sabedor de la falsedad de la imputación, o el que la hiciere de malicia, incurrirá en las penas de reclusión menor en sus grados mínimo a medio y multa de once a quince unidades tributarias mensuales.
articles.applicability_rationale: legacy paraphrase: El que imputare falsamente a alguna persona haber cometido un crimen o simple delito, siendo sabedor de la falsedad de la imputacion, incurrira en las penas de reclusion menor.

articles.article_name: Codigo Penal (CHIPENCOD), Art. 212 — Denuncia calumniosa / simulacion de victima
articles.article_text: El que simulare ser víctima de algún crimen o simple delito, o que en el parte o denuncia que diere a la autoridad supusiere haber intervenido personas que no han tenido participación en el hecho o que hubieren dejado rastros que puedan inducir a error sobre la perpetración de una acción delictiva, o que con igual propósito hiciere o facilitare que otro presente dichas circunstancias, sufrirá la pena de reclusión menor en su grado mínimo a medio o multa de seis a diez unidades tributarias mensuales.
articles.applicability_rationale: legacy paraphrase: Penalties for defamation and calumnia when made before authorities.

articles.article_name: Constitucion, Art. 19 N°4 — Prohibicion de constriccion ilegitima
articles.article_text: The application of any illegitimate constrain is forbidden;
articles.applicability_rationale: legacy paraphrase: Respect and protection of private life and honor.

articles.article_name: Ley 19.496, Art. 3(b) — Derecho a informacion veraz y oportuna
articles.article_text: b) El derecho a una información veraz y oportuna sobre los bienes y servicios ofrecidos, su precio, condiciones de contratación y otras características relevantes de los mismos, y el deber de informarse responsablemente de ellos.
articles.applicability_rationale: legacy paraphrase: Son derechos y deberes basicos del consumidor: b) El derecho a una informacion veraz y oportuna sobre los bienes y servicios ofrecidos, su precio, condiciones de contratacion y otras caracteristicas relevantes de los mismos.

articles.article_name: Ley 19.496, Art. 23 — Infraccion por negligencia del proveedor que causa menoscabo
articles.article_text: Comete infracción a las disposiciones de la presente ley el proveedor que, en la venta de un bien o en la prestación de un servicio, **actuando con negligencia**, causa menoscabo al consumidor debido a fallas o deficiencias en la calidad, cantidad, identidad, sustancia, procedencia, seguridad, peso o medida del respectivo bien o servicio.
articles.applicability_rationale: legacy paraphrase: El proveedor de un servicio sera responsable de los danos y perjuicios que cause al consumidor por la prestacion de un servicio defectuoso, incluyendo la falta de veracidad en la informacion proporcionada y el incumplimiento de las condiciones de contratacion.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Constitutional guarantee of equal protection of the law (due process)
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for Art. 19 Nº 3 of the Constitución Política de la República from bcn.cl/leychile and confirm it covers equal protection and due process rights
Confirm that the guarantee extends horizontally to private actors (eficacia horizontal) in the context of airline security procedures that effectively adjudicate passenger rights
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: Art. 19 Nº 3 guarantees equal protection of the law in the exercise of rights. Threats of 'more problems' if authorities are called could constitute a de facto denial of the passenger's right to seek legal recourse, implicating this guarantee. Horizontal application to a private airline requires careful analysis under Chilean constitutional doctrine.
candidate_articles.history_note: Carried forward from legacy import candidate list. Needs verbatim verification and horizontal-applicability analysis.

verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for Art. 296 of the Código Penal from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm whether the threat of 'more problems' if authorities are called meets the threshold of a conditional threat under Art. 296 numerals 1–3
Verify whether the threat must involve a serious evil (mal grave) or whether lesser threats are covered
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: Art. 296 CP penalizes conditional threats — i.e., threatening someone with an evil to compel them to do or refrain from doing something. The statement implying the passenger would face 'more problems' if he contacted authorities could constitute a conditional threat aimed at dissuading the exercise of a legal right. The key question is whether the language used meets the statutory threshold of seriousness.
candidate_articles.history_note: New candidate. The violation title explicitly references threats of 'more problems' if authorities are called, which maps directly to the conditional-threat typology in Art. 296 CP.

verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for Art. 297 of the Código Penal from bcn.cl/leychile
Determine whether Art. 297 applies as a residual category if Art. 296 threshold is not met
Confirm penalty range and whether it requires a formal complaint (querella) or proceeds de oficio
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: Art. 297 CP covers threats that do not meet the gravity threshold of Art. 296 but still constitute intimidation. If the 'more problems' language is deemed insufficiently grave for Art. 296, Art. 297 may serve as the applicable residual provision.
candidate_articles.history_note: New candidate. Companion to Art. 296 for lesser-gravity threats.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Coacción — impedir el ejercicio de derechos (coercion preventing exercise of rights)
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for Art. 161 of the Código Penal from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm whether Art. 161 covers private actors or only public officials — if it is limited to public officials, flag the agent-fit mismatch
Verify whether a separate coercion provision (e.g., Art. 494 Nº 16 on apremios ilegítimos by private persons) is more appropriate
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: AGENT-FIT CAUTION: Art. 161 CP may be limited to public officials who impede the exercise of rights. If so, it would not directly apply to LATAM airline security staff unless they were acting under delegated public authority at the airport. Verification of the article's subjective scope is essential before relying on it.
candidate_articles.history_note: New candidate. Included for completeness given the coercive nature of the conduct, but agent-fit mismatch is likely.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Falta de amenaza o coacción leve (minor-offense threat/coercion) — Código Penal
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for Art. 494 Nº 16 of the Código Penal from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm whether this falta covers threats or intimidation by private persons that do not rise to the level of Arts. 296–297
Verify penalty classification (falta vs. simple delito)
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: Art. 494 Nº 16 CP penalizes minor threats or intimidation as a falta. It may apply if the conduct does not meet the threshold for Arts. 296–297 but still constitutes punishable intimidation by a private actor.
candidate_articles.history_note: New candidate. Residual minor-offense provision for intimidation.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Fuerza como vicio del consentimiento (duress vitiating consent) — Código Civil
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for Art. 1457 of the Código Civil from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm that 'fuerza' includes moral intimidation (not only physical force)
Assess whether the passenger's acquiescence to deplaning or other airline demands was vitiated by the threats
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: Art. 1457 CC establishes that duress (fuerza) vitiates consent when it is capable of producing a strong impression on a reasonable person. If the passenger was coerced into accepting conditions (e.g., leaving the aircraft, not calling authorities) through threats of 'more problems,' any resulting agreement or waiver could be voidable for duress.
candidate_articles.history_note: New candidate. Civil-law dimension of the intimidation conduct.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Requisitos de la fuerza como vicio del consentimiento — Código Civil
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for Art. 1456 of the Código Civil from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm the three requirements for duress (grave, injusta, determinante) and whether the facts meet them
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: Art. 1456 CC sets out the requirements for duress to vitiate consent: it must be grave, unjust, and determinative. The threat of 'more problems' if authorities are called is arguably unjust (it seeks to prevent the exercise of a legal right) and determinative if it caused the passenger to refrain from calling authorities.
candidate_articles.history_note: New candidate. Companion to Art. 1457 CC on the civil-law duress analysis.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Responsabilidad extracontractual por hecho ilícito — Código Civil
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for Art. 2314 of the Código Civil from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm that intimidation causing moral harm (daño moral) is actionable under this provision
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: Art. 2314 CC establishes general tortious liability: whoever commits a wrongful act (delito o cuasidelito) that causes damage to another is obliged to indemnify. Intimidation causing moral harm (anxiety, humiliation) to the passenger would ground a civil claim under this article.
candidate_articles.history_note: New candidate. General tort provision for the civil damages dimension of the intimidation.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Reparación integral del daño — Código Civil
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for Art. 2329 of the Código Civil from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm that it establishes a presumption of culpability for imprudent or negligent conduct and full reparation
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: Art. 2329 CC complements Art. 2314 by establishing that all damage attributable to malice or negligence must be repaired. It also creates a presumption of fault in certain circumstances. The airline's intimidation conduct, if proven negligent or intentional, triggers full reparation including moral damages.
candidate_articles.history_note: New candidate. Companion to Art. 2314 for full-reparation principle.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Derecho a la libre elección del bien o servicio — Ley del Consumidor
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for Art. 3 letra a) of Ley 19.496 from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm whether the right to free choice encompasses the right not to be coerced into accepting degraded service conditions
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: Art. 3 letra a) LPC guarantees the consumer's right to free choice. Intimidation that pressures a passenger into accepting deplaning or forgoing complaints effectively negates free choice in the consumption of the air transport service.
candidate_articles.history_note: New candidate. Extends the consumer-rights analysis beyond Art. 3 letra b) already established.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Derecho a la reparación e indemnización adecuada — Ley del Consumidor
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for Art. 3 letra e) of Ley 19.496 from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm it covers the right to adequate reparation and indemnification for damages suffered
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: Art. 3 letra e) LPC establishes the consumer's right to adequate reparation and indemnification. Threats designed to dissuade the passenger from seeking redress directly undermine this statutory right.
candidate_articles.history_note: New candidate. The intimidation was specifically aimed at preventing the passenger from exercising his right to seek reparation.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Cláusulas abusivas — renuncia anticipada a derechos del consumidor
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for Art. 16 letra g) of Ley 19.496 from bcn.cl/leychile
Determine whether coerced verbal waivers (not just written contract clauses) fall within the scope of abusive-clause doctrine
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: Art. 16 letra g) LPC declares abusive any clause that causes an unjustified imbalance to the detriment of the consumer. If the airline's intimidation effectively extracted a waiver of the passenger's right to complain, this could be analyzed as an abusive practice analogous to an abusive clause. Applicability to oral coercion (rather than written terms) requires verification.
candidate_articles.history_note: New candidate. Extends abusive-clause analysis to coerced waivers.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Derechos del pasajero en caso de denegación de embarque — Código Aeronáutico
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for Art. 133 of the Código Aeronáutico (DFL Nº 221 de 1931 / Ley 18.916) from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm whether it establishes passenger rights when boarding is denied and whether it requires written justification
Verify the correct article number — the Código Aeronáutico's passenger-rights provisions may be in Arts. 131–135 range
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: Art. 133 CACH may establish the airline's obligations when denying boarding, including providing written reasons. The passenger's demand for written documentation ('¡Por escrito!') and the airline's intimidation to avoid providing it would directly implicate this provision.
candidate_articles.history_note: New candidate. The aeronautical code's boarding-denial provisions are directly relevant to the factual context.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Responsabilidad del transportador aéreo por daños al pasajero — Código Aeronáutico
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for Art. 147 of the Código Aeronáutico from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm whether it covers non-physical damages (moral harm) caused by the carrier's conduct during the transport operation
Verify the correct article number for carrier liability in the current consolidated text
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: Art. 147 CACH establishes the air carrier's liability for damages caused to passengers. If intimidation by airline security staff during the boarding/deplaning process constitutes actionable harm, this provision would ground the carrier's liability under aeronautical law.
candidate_articles.history_note: New candidate. Sectoral liability provision specific to air transport.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Derecho a la libertad personal y seguridad individual — Constitución
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for Art. 19 Nº 7 letra a) of the Constitución Política from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm whether the right to personal liberty and security encompasses protection against private intimidation that restricts freedom of action
Assess horizontal applicability to private airline conduct
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: Art. 19 Nº 7 letra a) CPR guarantees personal liberty and individual security. Threats of 'more problems' that effectively restrain the passenger's freedom to contact authorities or leave freely could implicate this guarantee. Horizontal application to a private airline requires analysis.
candidate_articles.history_note: New candidate. Constitutional dimension of the intimidation affecting personal liberty.

verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for Art. 19 Nº 14 of the Constitución Política from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm that the right of petition includes the right to contact authorities without retaliation
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: Art. 19 Nº 14 CPR guarantees the right to present petitions to any authority. Threatening a passenger with 'more problems' if he calls authorities directly obstructs this constitutional right.
candidate_articles.history_note: New candidate. The intimidation was specifically aimed at preventing the passenger from contacting authorities.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Multas por infracciones a la Ley del Consumidor
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for Art. 24 of Ley 19.496 from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm the penalty range for infractions and whether aggravating circumstances (intimidation) increase the sanction
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: Art. 24 LPC establishes the penalty framework for infractions of the consumer protection law. If the intimidation constitutes an infraction under Art. 23 (already established), Art. 24 provides the sanctioning mechanism and may allow enhanced penalties for the gravity of the conduct.
candidate_articles.history_note: New candidate. Sanctioning complement to the already-established Art. 23 LPDC.

open_questions.question: ¿Se presentó efectivamente una denuncia, parte policial o comunicación formal ante Carabineros, PDI, DGAC u otra autoridad competente contra el pasajero Leandro Disconzi? De existir, ¿quién fue el denunciante formal y cuál fue el contenido textual de la imputación?

¿Se le imputó al pasajero la comisión de un crimen o simple delito específico (e.g., desorden en aeronave, amenazas, resistencia) o la imputación se limitó a una infracción administrativa o reproche conductual genérico?
¿Existe un segmento de audio, video o testimonio adicional que contenga la amenaza explícita de 'más problemas si llama a las autoridades' referida en el título de la violación CL-019?

¿Existe un informe de seguridad interno de LATAM Airlines (Security Incident Report, bitácora de seguridad, o comunicación interna) que contenga afirmaciones sobre la conducta del pasajero y que haya sido remitido a alguna autoridad?

¿Existen comunicaciones internas de LATAM (correos electrónicos, mensajes, instrucciones de supervisores) que revelen la motivación real detrás de la imputación al pasajero o instrucciones de presionar/intimidar al pasajero?
¿Cuál es la relación contractual formal de Joaquín Barraza con LATAM Airlines? ¿Es empleado directo, contratista de seguridad o mandatario? ¿Cuál era su cargo y facultades al momento del incidente?

¿Qué ocurrió después de los eventos registrados en los segmentos? ¿El pasajero fue finalmente embarcado en el vuelo contratado, o se le denegó definitivamente el embarque? ¿Incurrió en gastos adicionales?

¿Se produjo la confrontación en un espacio público (gate, counter, zona de embarque) con presencia de terceros testigos? ¿Existen registros de video de las cámaras de seguridad del aeropuerto que acrediten la publicidad del acto?
¿Se inició alguna actuación policial o administrativa formal contra el pasajero (detención, control de identidad, anotación en registros) como consecuencia directa de la supuesta imputación falsa?

¿Existen protocolos internos de LATAM Airlines para el manejo de pasajeros conflictivos o denegación de embarque que permitan evaluar si la conducta de Barraza se desvió del estándar de diligencia exigible?
¿Se cuenta con el boleto aéreo, boarding pass o comprobante de compra que acredite formalmente la relación de consumo entre el pasajero y LATAM Airlines?

¿La imputación al pasajero fue presentada ante la autoridad como delito (desorden público, amenazas, interferencia con tripulación) o como mera infracción reglamentaria/administrativa, lo que determinaría la subsunción en Art. 211 o Art. 212 CP?
¿Se cuenta con peritaje psicológico, certificación médica u otra prueba que acredite el daño moral o extrapatrimonial sufrido por el pasajero como consecuencia de la intimidación?

¿La jurisprudencia de los Juzgados de Policía Local ha aplicado el Art. 23 LPDC a conductas de intimidación o trato indigno al consumidor, o estas se canalizan preferentemente por Art. 3 letra d) o Art. 16 LPDC?
¿Invocó LATAM Airlines alguna norma reglamentaria, protocolo de seguridad o cláusula contractual para justificar la restricción al pasajero o la conducta de su personal?
